tasks.title: Lecture #31
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a psychology podcast.
tasks.transcript: Woman: The placebo effect occurs when people experience real health improvements after receiving a treatment with no medical value—like a sugar pill—simply because they believe it’s real. Clinical trials use various placebos, including creams, gels, or even fake devices. It’s important that these are designed to closely resemble actual treatments. This ensures that participants can’t tell whether they’re receiving the real treatment or the placebo, which in turn keeps the study fair and the results scientifically reliable. The placebo effect highlights the powerful connection between mind and body. It’s influenced by factors such as patient expectations, how the treatment is delivered, and the provider’s credibility. In fact, a recent study found that when people expect relief, their brains respond as if real medicine has been given. This expectation alone can trigger specific brain activity, activating a pathway that links regions involved in thought, emotion, and movement. When these areas work together, they create a kind of bridge, connecting mind and body—mental belief and physical response. While placebos don’t actually cure diseases, the belief that a treatment will work can lead to real improvements in how a patient feels. So, when combined with actual medicine, I believe this psychological boost can enhance overall care.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: How scientists first discovered the placebo effect
options.B: How the brain drives the placebo effect
options.C: What types of medications are used in clinical trials
options.D: What role pharmaceutical companies play in placebo research

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者主要讨论了什么？ 定位原文： The placebo effect highlights the powerful connection between mind and body. ... In fact, a recent study found that when people expect relief, their brains respond as if real medicine has been given. This expectation alone can trigger specific brain activity, activating a pathway that links regions involved in thought, emotion, and movement. When these areas work together, they create a kind of bridge, connecting mind and body—mental belief and physical response. 选项分析： A. How scientists first discovered the placebo effect（科学家最初是如何发现安慰剂效应的）。讲话未讨论发现历史，所以A选项错误。 B. How the brain drives the placebo effect（大脑如何驱动安慰剂效应）。讲话重点解释了安慰剂效应的生理机制，特别是大脑如何通过预期触发特定脑区活动，在思维与身体反应之间建立连接，因此B选项正确。 C. What types of medications are used in clinical trials（临床试验中使用哪些类型的药物）。讲话提到临床试验使用各种安慰剂，但这不是主要内容，所以C选项错误。 D. What role pharmaceutical companies play in placebo research（制药公司在安慰剂研究中扮演什么角色）。讲话未提及制药公司，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about the various types of placebos?

options.A: They should be cheaper than the actual treatment.
options.B: They should be colorful and eye-catching.
options.C: They must undergo testing before clinical use.

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：演讲者对各类安慰剂提出了什么观点？ 定位原文： Clinical trials use various placebos, including creams, gels, or even fake devices. It’s important that these are designed to closely resemble actual treatments. This ensures that participants can’t tell whether they’re receiving the real treatment or the placebo... 选项分析： A. They should be cheaper than the actual treatment（它们应该比实际治疗更便宜）。讲话未提及成本比较，所以A选项错误。 B. They should be colorful and eye-catching（它们应该色彩鲜艳、引人注目）。讲话未提及外观颜色，所以B选项错误。 C. They must undergo testing before clinical use（它们在临床使用前必须经过测试）。讲话未提及测试要求，所以C选项错误。 D. They must resemble real treatments（它们必须与实际治疗相似）。讲话明确指出安慰剂的设计应尽可能接近实际治疗，以确保参与者无法区分，因此D选项正确。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker discuss “creating a kind of bridge”?

options.A: To illustrate how expectation can lead to physical response
options.B: To describe how medicine travels through the body
options.C: To clarify how emotions can block medical progress
options.D: To discuss the chemical composition of placebos

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者为什么讨论“创建一种桥梁”？ 定位原文： This expectation alone can trigger specific brain activity, activating a pathway that links regions involved in thought, emotion, and movement. When these areas work together, they create a kind of bridge, connecting mind and body—mental belief and physical response. 选项分析： A. To illustrate how expectation can lead to physical response（为了说明预期如何导致身体反应）。讲话用“桥梁”比喻大脑中思维、情感和运动区域的连接，说明仅凭预期就能触发大脑活动并产生身体反应，因此A选项正确。 B. To describe how medicine travels through the body（为了描述药物如何在体内运输）。讲话未讨论药物运输，所以B选项错误。 C. To clarify how emotions can block medical progress（为了阐明情绪如何阻碍医疗进展）。讲话未讨论情绪阻碍医疗进展，所以C选项错误。 D. To discuss the chemical composition of placebos（为了讨论安慰剂的化学成分）。讲话未涉及化学成分，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What is the speaker's opinion about the use of placebos in health care?

options.A: Placebos are not very relevant to patient care.
options.C: Placebos are only beneficial in psychological experiments.
options.D: Placebos should be studied more before being used in clinical settings.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者对安慰剂在医疗保健中的使用持什么看法？ 定位原文： While placebos don’t actually cure diseases, the belief that a treatment will work can lead to real improvements in how a patient feels. So, when combined with actual medicine, I believe this psychological boost can enhance overall care. 选项分析： A. Placebos are not very relevant to patient care（安慰剂与患者护理不太相关）。讲话认为安慰剂的心理促进作用可以增强整体护理，所以A选项错误。 B. Placebos can complement traditional therapies（安慰剂可以补充传统疗法）。讲话明确指出当安慰剂与实际药物结合使用时，可以增强整体护理，因此B选项正确。 C. Placebos are only beneficial in psychological experiments（安慰剂仅在心理实验中有益）。讲话认为在医疗保健中也有价值，所以C选项错误。 D. Placebos should be studied more before being used in clinical settings（安慰剂在用于临床环境之前应进行更多研究）。讲话未建议进一步研究，而是表达了其在现有医疗中的应用价值，所以D选项错误。
